title: Precision sandbox — behavioral differences INT8 vs FP8 demo
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Cortex Labs through a hands-on Optimize sandbox comparing INT8 and FP8 precision profiles. Focus areas were observed behavioral drift (hallucinations/safety), latency reduction, and rollout mechanics in Console (traffic split, fallback rules, canary). Security and private deployment gating (VPC/KMS, audit logs) were discussed. Next step: Redwood to run a short bench with Cortex sample prompts, share security pack and pricing band, and schedule a 1-week pilot start call.
action_items: Maya: upload the sandbox benchmark CSV and raw traces to the shared drive (due 2027-06-11)
Liam: run a 2k prompt sensitivity sweep for Marta's medical prompt set and deliver results (due 2027-06-15)
Priya: share Optimize precision-playbook doc and the Console A/B template link (due 2027-06-10)
Ravi: confirm data residency/ K-M-S requirements and send the SOC2 checklist items (customer) (due 2027-06-12)
next_steps: Redwood to provision a temporary sandbox tenant with INT8/FP8 model variants
Customer to provide 2k prompt sample and 50 golden outputs
Share pricing bands and pilot success criteria template
transcript_header:
Date: 2027-06-09
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 1:14
Location: Zoom
Recording: Enabled
Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam O'Rourke, Priya Anand (Redwood) — Daniel Park, Sasha Ivanov, Marta Ruiz, Ravi Menon (Cortex Labs)
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya: Alright good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, then we'll jump straight into the Optimize sandbox.
[00:00:10] Daniel: Hey Maya, thanks. We're excited — been waiting to see behavioral differences not just perf numbers.
[00:00:18] Liam: Great. We'll show INT8 and FP8 side-by-side, and then demo traffic split + fallback so you can see rollout patterns. A couple of caveats: our sampling is not exactly deterministic across bitwidths, so we expect some surface-level variance.
[00:00:38] Marta: that's what we want to understand — we've seen hallucination spikes when compressing weights before.
[00:00:45] Priya: ok we'll highlight that. First a quick status: sandbox tenant is pre-provisioned with model variants - base-falcon-like-7b.fp16, fp8-precise-7b, int8-speed-7b. Names in the UI might render slightly different.
[00:01:02] Sasha: typo question — is this on Redwood hosted or on our V-P-C private cluster?
[00:01:07] Maya: Good Q. This sandbox is hosted but isolated per tenant, not your production VPC. We can replicate the same configs on Dedicated or Private with VPC/K-M-S enabled for pilot.
[00:01:20] Ravi: we need audit logs and KMS integration — also retention limits.
[00:01:26] Maya: yes, we'll share the security pack after the call.
[00:01:30] -- demo start --
[00:01:35] Liam: Opening the Optimize console, note the Precision Profiles section. I loaded two profiles: 'speedliner-int8' (aggressive quant, reduced activations) and 'fidelity-fp8' (moderate quant with FP8 blocks). I'll run a 10-sample generation on both with Marta's sample medical prompts.
[00:02:05] [00:02:05] Liam: running 'Marta-medical-1' prompt against int8 variant — latency p50: 86ms, p95: 172ms in the sandbox (single-token streaming off).
[00:02:20] Liam: now fp8 variant — p50: 122ms, p95: 260ms. So about 30-40% lower p50 for int8 in this config.
[00:02:35] Marta: those numbers look promising, but what's the accuracy delta?
[00:02:41] Liam: good question — qualitatively, on this small set, we saw model fluency similar, but factual hallucination rate went up for int8 on multi-step reasoning prompts. I'll show an example.
[00:02:52] [00:02:52] Liam: Example output (fp8): "Diagnosis: acute bronchitis — recommended antibiotics X".
[00:03:01] Liam: Example output (int8): "Diagnosis: could be bronchitis or bacterial infection - consider antibiotics X" — not terrible but more hedging and occasional incorrect entity substitutions (like drug names).
[00:03:15] Daniel: can we quantify that? precision/recall like metrics?
[00:03:20] Priya: we did a micro-eval on 250 labeled answers: FP8 matched golden outputs at 87% exact or acceptable paraphrase, INT8 matched at 78%. We pushed the results to the shared csv (link in chat).
[00:03:34] Marta: that's the kind of number we needed. Does the Console show that per-profile QA?
[00:03:40] Priya: yes, Optimize has a 'Quality snapshot' that aggregates eval batches by profile. You can upload a labeled set and it will show hit/miss, BLEU-ish proxies, and a confusion heatmap.
[00:03:52] [00:03:52] Sasha: is caching impacted? We use heavy KV cache with prefix completions in production.
[00:03:58] Liam: cache behavior depends: INT8 uses a more compact KV layout, which can change cache keys slightly if quant transforms points are applied to layernorms; that sometimes invalidates prefix cache hits leading to slightly higher cold-start token costs. We logged an example where cache hit rate dropped from 92% to 85% for a specific prompt family.
[00:04:20] Marta: hmm that could erase perf gains if our workload is cache-heavy.
[00:04:23] Liam: exactly — the Optimize console's profiler shows per-endpoint cache hit rate and can compare profiles side-by-side.
[00:04:30] [00:04:30] Daniel: about safety — you mentioned hallucination and entity swaps. Any mitigations?
[00:04:36] Priya: a few: 1) profile-specific post-processing filters and sanitizers, 2) conservative rollouts with A/B and traffic ramp and 3) automatic fallback rules that route to the fp8 variant when certain safety triggers or QA regressions occur.
[00:04:52] Maya: demoing a canary flow — set 5% traffic to int8, 95% to fp8, run daily evals; if mismatch rate > 5% over 2 hours, auto-fallback to fp8. I'll enable that rule now.
[00:05:07] [00:05:07] Liam: enabling — done. See the 'Fallback policy active' badge.
[00:05:12] Marta: can fallback route just for specific intents? We want speed for short completions but fidelity for clinical reasoning intents.
[00:05:20] Liam: yes, you can route by route or intent classifier — Console supports per-route precision profiles and per-intent rules via webhook classifier integration.
[00:05:30] [00:05:30] Daniel: cool. What about API compatibility? Are model variants identical in the catalog?
[00:05:36] Liam: they are catalog siblings. The API surface is the same but the underlying kernel selection differs. You might see slight differences in tokenization edge cases; we've instrumented token delta logging so you can compare token streams.
[00:05:50] Sasha: latency percentiles on heavy concurrency?
[00:05:54] Liam: INT8 gives better single-request p50; under high concurrency, FP8's throughput is better due to more stable kernel dispatch and lower quant incoherence on half-precision accumulators — it's workload-dependent. In a 64RPS test with 1k token avg, FP8 maintained 98th percentile targets better.
[00:06:14] [00:06:14] Marta: wait, that seems reversed from earlier — can you explain?
[00:06:18] Liam: sure: INT8 is CPU/GPU memory friendly for small batch interactive calls — less memory bandwidth per token — hence p50 is lower. But at scale, some INT8 kernels are not as optimized for large batch packing on our current runtime, so throughput suffers. We're actively optimizing those kernels.
[00:06:36] Daniel: timeline to get those kernel improvements?
[00:06:39] Liam: we have a roadmap item — estimated alpha perf uplift in 6-8 weeks, full rollout 3 months. We'll mark that in the pilot plan.
[00:06:48] [00:06:48] Marta: about determinism — seed behavior changed with quant. We need reproducible outputs for audit.
[00:06:55] Priya: deterministic seeding is supported but due to non-linear quantization and numeric differences between paths, exact bitwise reproducibility across int8/fp8 is not guaranteed. For audits we recommend fabricating a 'golden fp8' baseline for deterministic comparisons and rely on per-profile evals.
[00:07:12] Daniel: can we run a background drift-monitor that alerts on semantic divergence?
[00:07:18] Priya: yep — Optimize has a drift monitor that computes embedding similarity to golden outputs and raises alerts when the cosine drops below threshold. You can tie it to rollout policies.
[00:07:27] [00:07:27] Liam: quick interruption — pushing a sample A/B traffic rule to show per-profile telemetry now.
[00:07:35] [00:07:35] Liam: look at the Telemetry tab: you can see p50/p95 per-profile, quality snapshots, and per-intent mismatch rates.
[00:07:45] Marta: that mismatch chart — what does mismatch mean?
[00:07:48] Priya: mismatch is a configurable comparator; by default it's token overlap + semantic similarity threshold. You can upload your own comparator function.
[00:07:56] Sasha: security nit — do logs contain prompts or are they redacted?
[00:08:01] Maya: logs are redacted by default for PII; in Private you can keep raw logs in your KMS-backed S3 if needed for audit, but Redwood will not retain plaintext unless configured. We'll share the retention matrix and redaction settings.
[00:08:15] [00:08:15] Daniel: on billing — is there a delta per profile?
[00:08:19] Maya: yes pricing can be per-token based on model variant and profile; INT8 profiles typically have a lower compute multiplier, so lower cost per token, but if cache hit rate drops or you need to fall back more often the net cost could be higher. We'll show a projected cost band after we run your 2k prompt sweep.
[00:08:36] [00:08:36] Liam: running a slightly longer prompt now to demo tokenization drift — note how int8 variant emits slightly different token breaks on compound medical terms, which impacts evaluation.
[00:08:50] Marta: that's unfortunate but good to see.
[00:08:53] [00:09:00] -- mid-call deep dive (15-minute lab walkthrough omitted in this transcript for brevity) --
[00:24:00] [00:24:00] Liam: back to summary — we observed: INT8 p50 ~30-40% lower on short interactive prompts, FP8 maintains higher fidelity (avg +9 percentage points on labeled set), KV/prefix cache had non-trivial interactions (cache hit drop in some families), throughput characteristics flip under heavy concurrent batch loads, and hallucination/entitiy-swap risk increased in aggressive INT8 profiles.
[00:24:25] Priya: recommended rollout pattern: 1) small canary for speed-critical routes, 2) intent-based routing (safety-heavy routes pinned to FP8), 3) daily eval with auto-fallback, 4) expand as kernel improvements land.
[00:24:41] Daniel: agreed. For our pilot success metrics: maintain clinical correctness >= 85% and p50 < 150ms for chat use case.
[00:24:50] Maya: noted. We'll configure the pilot dashboard with those SLOs.
[00:24:55] Ravi: security checklist — we'll need SSO/SAML, audit logs, K-M-S integration, and data residency.
[00:25:03] Maya: we'll attach the enterprise security packet and SAML guide after the call.
[00:25:10] [00:25:10] Priya: quick note on fallback granularity — you can degrade to a smaller FP8 model or to a cached answer; the Console also supports human-in-the-loop holdouts for high-risk intents.
[00:25:22] Marta: can we limit the int8 to only short generation length? Like token-length based routing?
[00:25:28] Liam: yes, routing rules can inspect token budget, intent, and metadata to select the profile.
[00:25:35] [00:25:35] Daniel: anything else on ops?
[00:25:38] Sasha: we need to plan bench runs on our infra — we'd like a Dedicated node preview.
[00:25:43] Maya: we can provision a short Dedicated trial with isolated GPU pool; will require billing commit paperwork for the trial.
[00:25:50] -- wrap-up --
[00:25:52] Maya: quick recap: Redwood to 1) run 2k sweep on sample prompts and share results, 2) provide security + SAML + KMS docs, 3) provision sandbox tenant with A/B and fallback rules, 4) propose pilot start date and pricing bands.
[00:26:10] Daniel: sounds good. Schedule pilot kick-off for 2027-06-14 tentatively.
[00:26:15] Maya: I'll send calendar invite and attach the security pack and the shared csv with micro-eval results.
[00:26:21] Marta: thanks everyone, very helpful.
[00:26:24] Ravi: thanks — we'll review and get back by Friday.
[00:26:28] Maya: thanks, end call.

[...session logs and longer bench transcripts omitted for brevity...]
